hints: Only the swaps' two values change positions, but round boundaries depend on adjacent value order.
Before swapping, identify the position comparisons for values x-1,x,x+1,y-1,y,y+1.
Subtract their old break contributions, swap positions, then add the new contributions; avoid counting the same comparison twice.
analogy: A swap only changes the local links in the chain of values being collected.
example: If 2 and 5 swap places, only comparisons around 1,2,3,4,5,6 can change; other position orderings stay identical.
algorithm: Store the array and inverse positions. For each swap, gather distinct adjacent-value pairs affected by the two values, remove their descent indicators, swap array positions, then add updated indicators and report rounds.
correctness: A round count is determined solely by each neighboring value pair's relative position; unaffected pairs keep their contribution, and the updated pairs are recomputed exactly.
complexity: O(q) time for a fixed number of affected pairs per query and O(n) space.
